findings.claim: The `open` row's verdict test is inverted (`s.review.lastVerdict !== "finding"`), so the ordinary code-finding repair path can never be selected and a live code finding falls through the whole table into the unclassified BLOCK.
findings.expected: Stage `review`, row `open` selected; effects DISPATCH{role: reviewer} -> WRITE{artifact: reviewLog, format: reviewResult} -> NEXT (exactly what fixtures/scenarios.json id "review-open" declares).
findings.actual: No row matches: `open` fails on `lastVerdict !== "finding"`; `broken-record` fails on `ordinal >= 3` (ordinal is 1); `replan` requires lastTarget "card-contract"; `undecided` requires "unverified"; `continue` and `unreviewed` require "pass"/"NONE". The stage is not done (done requires lastVerdict "pass" AND reviewLogPresent "yes"), so the table miss terminates as BLOCK:review-unclassified and the first code finding is never repaired.

findings.coordinate: spec.mjs:38 (TABLES.review.rows[0] "open", when predicate) together with TABLES.review.exclusive=false at spec.mjs:37
findings.claim: Because the inverted predicate makes `open` match every non-`finding` verdict whose target is "code", and `open` is the first row of a non-exclusive table, it shadows the `undecided` BLOCK row (and overlaps `continue`), silently converting a halt into forward progress.
findings.expected: Row `undecided` (when lastVerdict === "unverified") selected; effect BLOCK, because an unverified verdict is not evidence and must not advance the flow.
findings.actual: Row `open` also matches ("unverified" !== "finding" and lastTarget === "code") and is listed first in a table declared `exclusive: false`, so the flow instead runs DISPATCH{reviewer} -> WRITE{reviewLog} -> NEXT. The same shadowing hits `continue` (lastVerdict "pass", lastTarget "code", reviewLogPresent "no" matches both rows), which would re-dispatch a reviewer after a passing verdict, and it would swallow an out-of-vocabulary verdict such as "mystery" whenever lastTarget is "code" instead of blocking it.

findings.claim: `reviewLog` declares `readers: []` even though the review stage's own done predicate consumes it via `artifact.reviewLogPresent`, so the evidence artifact this skill exists to produce has no declared consumer.
findings.expected: readers should name at least `stage.review` (whose done predicate reads artifact.reviewLogPresent) and arguably `stage.route` (whose REPORT template has a "## Evidence" block citing it), matching how `signalRecord` on the adjacent line declares `readers: ["stage.signal"]`; READ_FIRST/`why: purpose` states evidence must survive session loss so a later agent can distinguish a completed review from a remembered claim.
findings.actual: `readers: []` declares the review log as a write-only sink. The write-then-read evidence loop that gates stage completion is undeclared, so nothing in the contract ties the log write to the `artifact.reviewLogPresent` observation that the stage's done condition depends on.

answers.answer: Stage `signal` is the next (active) stage and nothing is restricted. `signal.done` is `s.signal.pass === "yes"`, false here, so the flow does not advance; `session.readOnly` is "no", so the `read-only-session` guard (when readOnly === "yes" -> RESTRICT, forbids WRITE and DISPATCH) does not fire. The ordered effect plan is the stage's declared list, in order: (1) RUN {check: "completion"} - diagnose the failure in the completion result without inventing a pass; (2) WRITE {artifact: "signalRecord"} - append to state/signal.log (record kind: file, update: append, no format, template null); (3) NEXT. This matches fixtures/scenarios.json id "signal-open" (expect stage "signal", effects [RUN, WRITE, NEXT]). Stage `review` is not reached on this pass.

As authored, NO review row applies and the state terminates as BLOCK:review-unclassified - this is finding 1. Walking TABLES.review in order for (lastVerdict "finding", lastTarget "code", ordinal 1, disposition "NONE", reviewLogPresent "no"): `open` requires `lastVerdict !== "finding"` and fails; `broken-record` requires ordinal >= 3 and fails at 1; `replan` requires lastTarget "card-contract"; `undecided` requires "unverified"; `continue` requires "pass"; `unreviewed` requires "NONE". Stage `review` is the active stage (signal is done at signal.pass "yes"; review.done requires lastVerdict "pass" AND reviewLogPresent "yes"), so the table miss is the terminal result. The intended answer - and what the skill's own fixture "review-open" declares - is row `review/open` with ordered effects DISPATCH {role: "reviewer"} -> WRITE {artifact: "reviewLog", format: "reviewResult"} -> NEXT, unrestricted because session.readOnly is "no".

The broken-record boundary wins; the effect is the single ASK. At ordinal 3 the `broken-record` row's full conjunction holds (lastVerdict "finding" AND lastTarget "code" AND ordinal >= 3 AND disposition "NONE"), and it is the row named by the stage's `cycle: { counter: "review.ordinal", boundedBy: "broken-record" }`, so the cycle bound takes precedence over the ordinary repair path rather than dispatching a fourth reviewer - matching fixture "broken-record" (status ASK). Caveat: in this artifact the boundary wins vacuously rather than by precedence, because the inverted `open` predicate (finding 1) prevents the ordinary repair path from matching a code finding at any ordinal, so this state question cannot distinguish a correctly arbitrated bound from a dead repair path. The disposition term is what releases the bound: with `review.disposition` = "present", `broken-record` stops matching and - once `open` is repaired to `lastVerdict === "finding"` - the ordinary repair path resumes.

It terminates as a BLOCK - not via a default row, and not by falling through to the next stage. "mystery" is inside the declared domain of `review.lastVerdict` but is matched by no row: `open` needs lastTarget "code" (it is "NONE"), `broken-record` and `replan` need "finding", `undecided` needs "unverified", `continue` needs "pass", `unreviewed` needs "NONE". TABLES.review declares no default/catch-all row and `exclusive: false` does not supply one, and stage `review` is not done (done requires lastVerdict "pass" AND reviewLogPresent "yes"), so the unmatched state halts as BLOCK:review-unclassified - the result fixture "unclassified" declares. No DISPATCH, WRITE, or NEXT is presented; the flow stops until the verdict is classified into the vocabulary shared by FORMATS.reviewResult and ROLES.reviewer.judgments (`pass`, `finding`, `unverified`). Note that this clean termination depends on lastTarget being "NONE": because of finding 2, the same "mystery" verdict with lastTarget "code" would be captured by the inverted `open` row and dispatched instead of blocked.

No. `session.readOnly` is "yes", so the `read-only-session` guard fires (when readOnly === "yes" -> RESTRICT, forbids ["WRITE", "DISPATCH"]), and its body directs the skill to explain that the session can inspect but cannot present a state-changing plan. This state would otherwise land on stage `review`, row `unreviewed` (lastVerdict "NONE"; `open` does not match because lastTarget is "NONE", not "code"), whose effects are DISPATCH {role: "reviewer"} -> WRITE {artifact: "reviewLog"} -> NEXT - the first two are exactly the forbidden pair, so that plan may not be presented. Only non-forbidden effects remain available (inspection and reporting: RUN, ASK, ROUTE, REPORT). The guard restricts presentation of the plan; it does not silently downgrade it to a WRITE-less and DISPATCH-less variant that would advance state on weaker evidence.

notes: Method: read only review-brief.md, state-questions.json, review-output.schema.json, and the seven files of evals/g0_5/b-v5-mutated; ran only the permitted lint command; no oracle, controls, A form, docs, history, or other results were consulted. Root cause of findings 1 and 2 is a single inverted comparison in TABLES.review row `open` (`!==` where the row's own semantics, the stage body "Repair code findings; leave card-contract findings to planning", the cycle bound on `broken-record`, and fixtures/scenarios.json id "review-open" all require `===`); repairing it to `s.review.lastVerdict === "finding" && s.review.lastTarget === "code"` resolves both, and the resulting overlap with `broken-record` at ordinal >= 3 is exactly what `exclusive: false` plus the declared cycle bound exist to arbitrate. Lint output was deliberately not treated as a clean bill of health: the run exits 1 on L0 (spec import failure, spec: null) while still reporting L1-L18 as "pass", so no lint check actually evaluated this spec - see finding 4. Two things were examined and deliberately NOT reported as defects: (a) every collector in collectors/index.mjs returns the literal "UNKNOWN", which is outside each observation's declared domain - uniform across all seven collectors, so it reads as fixture scaffolding driven by scenarios.json rather than an authored defect, though it would stall every predicate if a runtime consumed it as-is; (b) `replan: ["ROUTE:planning"]` targets a skill absent from SPEC.imports (`[]`) under profile "single", but the review stage body explicitly delegates card-contract findings to planning, so it appears intended and no fixture covers the row. Coverage gap worth flagging to the maintainer: fixtures/scenarios.json exercises only 3 of the 6 table rows and neither the `route` stage nor the `read-only-session` guard, so rows `replan`, `undecided`, `continue`, and `unreviewed` have no mechanical check at all - which is why finding 2's shadowing of `undecided` and `continue` would still not surface in the fixture suite even after finding 1 is fixed.
